summary: G0-G3 completed; R1 capability audit starts without an algorithm hypothesis or quality claim.
Two optimization frontends are executable and three feed-forward paths are adaptable. The first dirty-source run is noncanonical; clean-source fail-closed execution produced the canonical R1 run.

A real StreetGS checkpoint with 1,267,870 Gaussians and a ReconDrive output-schema fixture both round-trip through SceneIR v0 within the frozen tolerance and reload in fresh processes. This establishes only the representation interface, not reconstruction quality.

Across two development scenes and StreetGS/AD-GS, deviation produced stable measurable failure structure, but the preregistered analytic support certificate did not outperform lateral distance and its equal-distance residual rank was below gate. Learned support is rejected; distance remains a benchmark descriptor, not a universal validity certificate. Actor and forward probes remain effect evidence only.

The same real StreetGS SceneIR package produced exact world state, labels, chunk selection, 23-actor trajectories, and uint8 compiler-diagnostic RGB in three isolated fresh processes. No visual tolerance, GPU, training, or confirmation data was used. This passes the compiler determinism gate but is not a photorealistic source-camera quality result.

All 24 chunks, 23 actors and 1,267,870 primitives receive six typed provenance fields with exact fresh reload. Every current primitive is reconstructed, none is observed or generated, and absent sensor/view support remains unknown. Primitive identity must be composite over chunk_id and local source_index.

On all 48 frozen R3 rows, task-conditioned photo/geometry/semantic validity accepted only 8.3%/29.2%/8.3% but had zero accepted failures; the R3 single scalar reached 50% worst-case false-safe. Dynamics correctly accepted no cases because no independent dynamics verifier exists. This is a development proxy result, not confirmation calibration.

On 28 evidence-eligible pseudo-holes, every exact oracle proposal passed, every matched corrupted control failed, masked photo/depth errors recovered exactly, and outside-mask values and provenance were preserved. Four scene-0048/StreetGS actor cases had exactly zero actor-edit evidence and remain structural ABSTAIN. This validates only the observation-plane oracle upper-bound integration path.

Big-LaMa and SD-v1.5 each completed four frozen pseudo-holes twice with exact repeat hashes, finite nonzero masked change and exact outside-mask overlays. Big-LaMa was selected by the preregistered resource order at 428 MiB and 0.0374 seconds median versus SD at 2718 MiB and 0.786 seconds. This is capability only; no generated pixel is verified or baked.

On 28 matched pseudo-holes Big-LaMa produced no photo or geometry accepts; its semantic arm accepted 6 of 12 actor-evidence cases but one was false-safe, exceeding the frozen 0.10 ceiling. Dynamics correctly abstained on all 28. Resource and non-target gates passed, so the next isolated variable is the already capability-qualified SD-v1.5 generator with all verifier thresholds unchanged.

With every verifier threshold unchanged, SD-v1.5 produced zero photo accepts, only two geometry accepts out of 28, and the same one-in-six semantic false-safe as Big-LaMa; dynamics abstained on all cases. This rejects the second single-image generator and motivates an aligned cross-frontend reconstructed proposal, not threshold relaxation or per-case generator mixing.

Replacing single-image hallucination with a same-frame, same-edit reconstruction from the other frozen frontend yields independently valid photo and geometry arms: 10/28 and 3/28 accepts with zero false-safe. Semantic remains ineligible at one false-safe among six accepts and dynamics remains all-abstain. R10 may fuse only photo and geometry, and the shared sensor-support boundary remains explicit.

Fusing only independently valid photo and geometry arms yields 3 ACCEPT, 7 ABSTAIN and 18 REJECT over 28 cases, with zero false-safe and 9.52% verified mask area. All seven arm disagreements become ABSTAIN. Semantic, dynamics and verified trajectory length remain explicitly unsupported, so R11 must type-check assets before bake.

R11 packages the two jointly photo-and-geometry-valid route proposals as explicit sparse RGB chunks and reloads both exactly without a generator. The factor-incomplete actor hole becomes a bake ABSTAIN, producing zero actor and trajectory assets. R12 can validate only the resulting static logged-support sensor path until independently valid dynamic evidence exists.

Both baked static chunks replay twice with zero RGB error against their frozen source proposals, exact repeat hashes and exact frozen DeepLab label hashes. Peak GPU memory is 394 MiB and wall time 5.7 seconds. This closes only static sensor/perception consistency; all dynamic, event and calibration dimensions remain unsupported, so the next hypothesis uses the frozen SceneIR conformance package rather than manufacturing fields in the R11 package.

The frozen ReConDrive SceneIR fixture fresh-loads twice and produces exact actor world states, trajectories, camera calibration, actor semantic classes and AABB collision labels for two actors at two timestamps. This validates the interface contract but not real-scene scale or physical accuracy; H-R12-003 therefore moves to the real StreetGS scene-0230 package while retaining calibration/event abstentions where unsupported.

StreetGS scene-0230 fresh-replays all 23 actors and 4508 trajectory rows over 196 timestamps twice with exact actor, trajectory, semantic-class and 49588 AABB collision-label outputs in 4.38 seconds. Real-scene sensor calibration and events remain absent. R13 now tests whether the verified static patches can be lifted from their 2D bake format into sparse world-space route support.

The first lift creates 58273 deterministic points and retains zero V6 false-safe, but its estimated 0.01993 m2 area and zero visible pixels at every nonzero deviation show that R9 verifier-relative depth is not metric camera z. Threshold relaxation is disallowed. The next hypothesis changes only depth to bounded same-frame logged LiDAR while preserving the complete comparison and gate.

Changing only the transport depth to bounded logged LiDAR yields 57997 points over an estimated 19.13 m2. Both keyframes pass 0.5m, 1m, 2m and 3m lateral plus 2m forward under unchanged gates; both 5m cases fail with geometry MRE near 9. V6 retains 0/3 false-safe versus 23/28 naive and 28/28 Big-LaMa. H-R13-003 tests whether adjacent-keyframe union fixes the 5m support gap before adding target-view visibility logic.

The pre-registered 5cm two-keyframe union collapses 57997 input points to 5868, regresses common lateral support from 3m to 2m and worsens mean 5m geometry MRE from 9.0572 to 10.6579. This is an occlusion/visibility mechanism failure, not a tunable voxel-size or resource failure. H-R13-004 returns to the accepted per-frame chunks and uses only frozen target-view three-camera logged LiDAR to reject contradicted points before unchanged evaluation.

The frozen target-view LiDAR filter preserves the accepted 3m route and exact/safety contracts, but retains about 78% of old points at 5m and leaves geometry MRE at 9.03/9.41, so deletion-only visibility cannot synthesize newly exposed surfaces. Direct observation shows projected metric LiDAR z medians near 13m while the StreetGS 5m depth proxy median is only 1.2-1.3, so the proxy is not valid metric truth at that extrapolation. The route scope is therefore closed at the independently achieved 3m lateral/2m forward limit; H-R13-005 moves to the plan's untested typed actor edit dimensions instead of tuning visibility thresholds against a broken 5m proxy.

All three real-scene typed edits compile exactly over 23 actors and 196 timestamps: removal deletes 655 positive AABB collisions, +20m trajectory translation has zero centroid error, and the added density clone creates exactly 196 new source-clone collisions. All unaffected actor states and collision pairs remain exact, V6 is 3/3 ACCEPT with zero false-safe, and the stale-dependency naive arm is 3/3 false-safe. This establishes functional dependency closure but not sensor/perception behavior, so H-R13-006 now consumes the already frozen two-frontend actor-removal renders and frozen DeepLab model.

After correcting AD-GS RGB range handling, all four actor-removal renders show strong RGB locality (224x-498x enrichment and outside MAE below 0.0004), but full-frame DeepLab changes 6.3%-10.3% of labels outside the actor support; only one case reaches the frozen 2x perception-locality gate. Threshold relaxation is forbidden. H-R13-007 changes the mechanism to independently inferred target/static ROIs selected only from logged actor opacity, while preserving the same RGB and semantic change thresholds and retaining the H-R13-006 full-frame rejection.

The frozen 256px/128px ROI selector finds high-actor target tiles, but even the minimum non-overlapping static candidates contain 9.9%-37.3% actor pixels because the operation removes every actor. All four cases therefore fail the pre-registered static-factor denominator before any perception benefit can be claimed. No tile/stride sweep is allowed. H-R13-008 changes the edit granularity by selecting one StreetGS actor from frozen visibility/point-count metadata and rendering only its removal, with AD-GS and SceneIR identity binding explicitly abstaining.

StreetGS model index 2 is selected without outcome access from 12 actors visible at both frames and contains 13490 Gaussians. Its logged rerender exactly matches frozen R3 and its removal is strongly RGB-local, but DeepLab target label change is only 0%-0.068%, below the frozen 2% effect gate. This rejects Gaussian count as a perception-sensitivity selector. H-R13-009 removes every eligible actor in a complete fixed denominator and uses factorized ACCEPT/ABSTAIN coverage under identical thresholds, avoiding another heuristic or threshold sweep.

The complete 12-actor denominator identifies exactly one actor (StreetGS model index 0) that passes unchanged two-frame sensor/perception locality gates. Verified coverage is 1/12=8.33%; V6 abstains on 11 actors with zero false-safe, while naive all-accept is 91.67% false-safe. This is deliberately sparse, not a broad success claim. H-R13-010 now converts the identical scene-0242 checkpoint to SceneIR and binds accepted model index 0 to actor_0000 so typed removal and sensor/perception evidence share one scene and identity.

H-R13-010 passed same-scene checkpoint binding, model index 0 to actor_0000/12390-primitives identity, fresh replay, all unaffected factor checks, package/source immutability and inherited V6 false-safe zero. It was nevertheless correctly rejected because the preregistration conflated H-R13-009's 12 actors visible in both frames with the checkpoint converter's 27 total SceneIR actors. V6-F40 records the bookkeeping failure. H-R13-011 changes only the pre-registered total denominators to the deterministic frozen converter outputs 27/26, 5292/5096 and 68796/63700; all mechanisms and quality thresholds remain unchanged.

H-R13-011 separates the converter's 27 total actors from H-R13-009's 12 two-frame-visible evaluation actors and passes every frozen gate. Model index 0 binds to actor_0000/12390 primitives in scene-0242; typed removal yields 27→26 actors, 5292→5096 trajectories and 68796→63700 collision rows, with exact fresh replay and unaffected factors. Together with route, dynamic edit and sparse perception results, R13 closes on a bounded development scope and explicitly abstains beyond it. The V6.4 regression-test-set option is now exercised by H-PT1-001 using scene-0230 as contract source and scene-0242 as an independent downstream scenario.

The first H-PT1-001 run stopped before loading the heldout replay or constructing mutations because the consumer expected the shortened decision key accept_typed_dynamic_edits while the frozen H-R13-005 gate uses accept_typed_dynamic_edit_dependency_closure. V6-F41 records the cross-stage schema failure. The repair moves both exact accepted decision strings into the frozen config and changes no mutation, arm, metric, threshold, resource or evidence contract; H-PT1-001 remains active for an independent rerun.

On the independent scene-0242 actor-removal episode, Real-only detects 0/4 frozen stale-factor regressions with false-safe 1.0, naive synthetic detects only stale actor_states (1/4) with false-safe 0.75, and the V6 verified compiled contract detects 4/4 with false-safe zero while all three accept the clean episode. Exact repeated evaluation holds. This is regression-test utility only. H-PT2-001 now tests whether recomputed typed-edit labels improve a minimal CONTINUE/BRAKE risk admission policy on whole-scene heldout scene-0255.

H-PT2-001 passes its incomplete numeric gate and defeats naive stale-label training, but Real-only also reaches heldout balanced accuracy 1.0 and false-safe zero despite zero positive training examples. The signed-clearance feature is exactly the verifier statistic, so the model family receives the answer boundary and cannot prove post-training data utility. V6-F42 records the leakage. H-PT2-002 preserves data and labels but exposes only raw relative forward/lateral positions, makes one-class policies constant, and adds a mandatory false-safe reduction gate versus both Real-only and naive.

H-PT2-002 removes verifier-statistic leakage and makes both Real-only and naive constant-CONTINUE with heldout false-safe 1.0. V6 learns a 3.0m/0.5m raw-position rectangle, reduces false-safe to 0.1122 and keeps safe-route completion 1.0, but misses the strict <=0.05 and >=0.95 gates. All 11 misses are exactly the 3m clones whose transformed feature is 1e-13 to 5e-13 above 3.0. V6-F43 records the numeric contract failure. H-PT2-003 adds only 1e-9m feature canonicalization while preserving labels, grids and gates.

With 1e-9m representation canonicalization only, H-PT2-003 learns a 3.0m forward/0.0m lateral rectangle from raw positions and recomputed V6 edit labels. On whole scene0255, it detects 98/98 hazards, continues on 147/147 safe rows and reduces false-safe from 1.0 for both Real-only and naive to zero; repeats are exact. The scope is still the zero-lateral intervention family. H-PT3-001 freezes the policy and evaluates unseen off-axis edits on new scene0048 before any broader policy claim.

On new scene0048 with 441 nonzero-lateral edit rows, the frozen PT2 V6 policy detects 0/232 hazards and false-safes at 1.0, identical to Real-only and naive. Exact repeats and source hashes pass, so this is a method rejection, not engineering drift. V6-F44 records that a zero-lateral edit denominator learns a zero-width intervention template. H-PT3-002 trains on a complete two-dimensional edit grid and evaluates a disjoint half-offset grid on the same new scene without relaxing robustness gates.

H-PT3-002 adds complete forward/lateral training coverage and reduces heldout false-safe from 1.0 to 0.4505 with completion 1.0, but fails the frozen robustness gates. Diagnostics show position-only nearest-actor features alias different projected box extents/orientations; exact 2m boundary labels also mix numerically. V6-F45 records the representation failure. H-PT3-003 keeps the data/gates and trains separate raw position+projected-half-extent overlap heads with 1e-9 factor-label canonicalization, then ANDs their predictions.

H-PT3-003 uses raw box extents and factor heads, improves heldout hazard recall to 0.7786, but false-safe 0.2214, safe-route completion 0.8140 and balanced accuracy 0.7963 miss the frozen gates. Train factor accuracy is near-perfect, indicating extrapolation rather than optimization failure: one default synthetic size/yaw cannot identify extent coefficients robustly. V6-F46 records the coverage gap. H-PT3-004 expands only the training intervention denominator across size and yaw and evaluates disjoint size/yaw combinations on scene0048.

H-PT3-004 expands train coverage to 23,520 synthetic interventions across size and yaw and evaluates 8,820 disjoint heldout interventions. V6 improves to balanced accuracy 0.8561 and false-safe 0.1482 versus 0.9713/1.0 for the baselines, but completion 0.8605 and the original gates still fail. The lateral factor train set is 88.17% positive, while unweighted BCE optimizes frequency-weighted accuracy instead of the frozen balanced metric. V6-F47 records this objective mismatch. H-PT3-005 changes only each factor head to equal-total-weight positive/negative BCE.

H-PT3-005 keeps the full intervention denominator and gives each factor class equal BCE weight, but heldout V6 balanced accuracy falls to 0.8229 and false-safe rises to 0.2475; the naive baseline also changes to 0.6786 false-safe, so its required reduction fails. Both V6 factor heads still have nonzero train error. V6-F48 records that loss reweighting is not a separating-margin mechanism. H-PT3-006 keeps all evidence and gates fixed but uses deterministic class-balanced linear max-margin heads on the same raw features.

H-PT3-006 max-margin heads reach exact V6 factor and joint train balanced accuracy and lower heldout false-safe to 0.0523, passing that gate with >0.62 reduction versus both baselines. Balanced accuracy is narrowly 0.8978 while completion is 0.8479 because the coarse train position lattice permits a conservative separator between points. V6-F49 records the support-resolution failure. H-PT3-007 densifies only the train position denominator with values disjoint from the unchanged heldout grid.

H-PT3-007 trains on 155,232 disjoint-support interventions and reaches heldout scene0048 balanced accuracy 0.9916, false-safe 0.0168 and safe-route completion 1.0. Real-only and naive false-safe remain 0.7149/0.6484; all source, repeat, resource, abstention and incremental gates pass. The adaptive development family is now frozen by exact artifact hashes. H-PT4-001 consumes one untouched scene0071 confirmation attempt with factor levels disjoint from both training and development heldout levels.

The exact frozen H-PT3-007 policy attains balanced accuracy 1.0, false-safe 0 and completion 1.0 on 8,869 scene0071 confirmation rows using factor levels disjoint from development. Real-only and naive false-safe are 0.7021/0.6064. The attempt was created before quality read, exact evaluation and source hashes pass, and the confirmation is consumed. H-PT5-001 freezes both candidate and accepted confirmation gate for a final exact-once scene0317 test.

The exact-once scene0317 test uses a third factor grid disjoint from development and confirmation and gives the frozen V6 arm balanced accuracy 1.0, false-safe 0 and completion 1.0 on 8,688 rows. Real-only/naive false-safe are 0.7233/0.6654; all attempt, prior-gate, source, repeat and abstention contracts pass. The single-clone family is permanently closed. H-PT6-001 starts an independent development task from its already-declared compositional scope gap, evaluating two simultaneous clones by per-actor set aggregation without changing the tested policy.

On 784 scene0450 two-clone episodes, frozen V6 is perfect on balanced accuracy, false-safe and completion, while Real-only underbrakes every hazard and naive detects 91.16% of hazards by false-braking 86.73% of safe episodes. The original >=0.50 false-safe reduction versus naive is therefore impossible because naive false-safe is only 0.0884. H-PT6-001 remains rejected under its gate. V6-F50 records the evaluation pathology; H-PT6-002 freezes all evidence and replaces only the cross-arm comparison with two-axis Pareto dominance plus a 0.20 balanced-accuracy gain.

H-PT6-002 preserves the exact 784 scene0450 episodes and absolute gates, and verifies that frozen V6 has 1.0 balanced accuracy, 0 false-safe and 1.0 completion while Pareto-dominating Real-only and naive; balanced-accuracy gains are 0.50 and 0.4779. Because the paired protocol was developed after H-PT6-001 exposed an infeasible comparison, H-PT7-001 freezes policy, gate and case denominator for one-shot confirmation on new scene0862 with disjoint clone tuples.

The frozen scene0862 one-shot composition confirmation preserves 1.0 safe completion and 0.9233 balanced accuracy, but V6 false-safe is 0.1533 and misses the frozen <=0.10 gate. The attempt, policy, prior gate, source, disjoint cases and repeats are valid, so this is a method rejection; V6-F51 records it. The candidate family is closed and cannot use confirmation outcomes for tuning. H-PT8-001 starts an independent family from the long-standing ABSTAIN_NO_LONGITUDINAL_CONTROLLER scope, evaluating a preregistered finite-horizon kinematic preview controller with the earlier immutable per-actor policy.

H-PT8-001 evaluates 360 five-second scenarios and finds V6 collision 0.25, safe completion 0.9375, comfort 1.0 and balanced accuracy 0.84375, identical to Real-only; naive is worse. All 70 V6 collisions occur at <=25m and are strongly concentrated at 8-10m/s and large actors, suggesting physical stopping infeasibility. V6-F52 records the unstratified denominator and the independent lack of Real-only gain. H-PT8-002 adds only a t=0 full-brake oracle feasibility stratum while retaining every scenario, model, controller and gate.

H-PT8-002 identifies 210 oracle-avoidable and 70 unavoidable hazards. V6 has zero collision on the avoidable stratum, 0.9375 safe completion and 0.96875 balanced accuracy, but Real-only is exactly identical because the earlier factorized arm receives enough real box overlap supervision to solve this static AABB preview task. The strong baseline is retained and the closed-loop family remains rejected; V6-F53 records the no-gain result. H-R14-001 returns to the core compiler's pre-existing proposal-evidence gap by testing adjacent-frame masked ECC reconstruction under unchanged R9 verifier arms.

On the unchanged 28-case R9 denominator, same-frontend adjacent-frame ECC proposals give P1 coverage 0.3929 and P2 coverage 0.1429 with zero false-safe and large reductions versus accept-all; both arms pass unchanged gates. P3 retains the known 0.1667 false-safe and P4 remains all-abstain. Source, outside-mask and resource checks pass at 424MiB peak. H-R15-001 consumes only P1/P2 for deterministic conjunction/disagreement abstention before any bake claim.

R15 consumes only independently valid R14 P1/P2 decisions and preserves zero false-safe, exact disagreement abstention and all governance checks, but their intersection is 1/28 (0.0357), below the frozen 0.05 gate; 13 cases disagree. H-R15-001 remains rejected and V6-F54 records that arm-wise validity is not sufficient for joint usable coverage. H-R16-001 changes only temporal proposal alignment to observed outside-mask RGB+render inverse-depth, leaving verifier thresholds and later conjunction untouched.

On the unchanged 28-case denominator, equal-weight outside-mask RGB plus render inverse-depth ECC proposals retain independently eligible P1/P2 with zero false-safe: P1 coverage rises from 0.3929 to 0.4286 while P2 changes from 0.1429 to 0.1071. P3 remains rejected at 0.1667 false-safe and P4 all-abstains. R17 now applies the frozen conjunction to determine whether alignment changed overlap rather than inferring joint validity from marginal arm gates.

The unchanged R16 P1/P2 conjunction produces two joint ACCEPTs (0.0714 coverage and 0.0515 usable mask area), zero false-safe and 11 correctly abstained disagreements, passing every R17 gate. Both accepts are typed static missing_route_support cases. R18 therefore packages only those two static chunks and keeps actor/trajectory assets absent because semantic and dynamics remain ABSTAIN.

R18 accounts for both R17 ACCEPTs as sparse static chunks totaling 58,273 pixels. Both reload to their full R16 proposals exactly, source hashes remain immutable and the package records complete provenance/validity with no online generator, model or network dependency. No actor or trajectory asset is emitted. R19 now tests downstream RGB replay and frozen perception repeatability from the package.

R19 reconstructs both compiled proposals exactly on two repeats each (RGB MAE 0 and identical array hashes) and yields repeat-identical frozen Deeplab label arrays, with 394MiB peak and 5.88s wall time. This closes the bounded static package chain but leaves semantic correctness, actor dynamics and full LogSim explicitly unsupported. R20 changes semantic evidence via a frozen DeepLab/SegFormer architecture consensus rather than retuning the rejected P3 threshold.

R20 retains 2/12 accepts but one is a false-safe disocclusion where DeepLab and SegFormer strongly agree (IoU 0.8827) on dynamic content even though the frozen truth is unsafe. False-safe rate 0.50 and reduction 0.0833 fail gates. V6-F55 records that architecture diversity does not make errors independent. R21 adds compiler edit-type semantics while reusing the original 0.50 actor consensus threshold and requiring strict dynamic absence for disocclusion.

R21 accepts 2/12 actor-related cases, with zero false-safe and 0.5833 reduction versus accept-all; strict disocclusion dynamic absence rejects the R20 correlated error. However both semantic ACCEPT proposals are photo/geometry REJECT under R16, so immediate three-factor fusion would have zero actor coverage. R22 changes the actor proposal mechanism by registering adjacent-frame actor edit support to the declared target hole mask, while retaining all verifier thresholds and non-actor RGB-D ECC proposals.

R22 preserves all global/static results and makes actor P2 eligible at 1/6 with zero false-safe, but actor P1 accepts 0/6. Four actor cases are photo truth-safe yet their proposal MAE remains 0.0630-0.0765 versus frozen 0.05. V6-F56 records that axis-aligned mask moments lack rotation/shear/perspective texture correspondence. R23 performs one signed-distance mask homography ECC from the same content-free edit-support evidence.

R23 remains actor P1 0/6 and P2 1/6; a more flexible mask homography often increases texture error because mask outline does not identify cross-time pose, visible surface or lighting. V6-F57 closes the mask-fitting route. H-R24-001 uses a typed, non-learned source router between prior accepted H-R16 temporal RGB-D static proposals and H-R9-003 same-time cross-frontend actor proposals.

R24 reproduces actor P1 4/6 and P2 1/6 with zero false-safe, while retaining global P1/P2 eligibility. It is nevertheless rejected because P1's accept-all false-safe rate is only 1/6, so the inherited 0.25 rate reduction cannot be reached even by zero false-safe. V6-F58 records the small-denominator gate defect. R25 keeps R24 rejected and tests a discrete strict reduction of at least one P0 false-safe per arm with unchanged absolute gates.

R25 evaluates immutable R24 outputs without new inference and accepts both actor arms: P1 removes the sole P0 false-safe and P2 removes both, while each has zero false-safe and nonzero coverage. R24 remains rejected. R26 now reruns the frozen R21 typed semantic contract on the exact R24 multisource proposals under R25 authority, so any later conjunction uses co-measured factor decisions rather than cross-run overlap assumptions.

R26 accepts 3/12 semantic-evidence proposals with zero false-safe and 0.5833 reduction versus accept-all using the unchanged R21 typed contract. One actor case, scene-0242 streetgs frame57, is simultaneously accepted by R24 P1/P2 and R26 P3 and is truth-safe; the sole truth-unsafe actor case is rejected by all three. R27 now measures this pre-registered conjunction and leaves dynamics explicit ABSTAIN.

The first R27 formal run failed before gate construction because R24 PER_CASE_ARMS does not carry mask_pixel_count. V6-F59 records the artifact-schema ownership error. The retry binds the already immutable R24 CASES.jsonl hash and reads only mask_pixel_count from its case index; factor decisions, truth labels, fusion, thresholds and expected outcome remain unchanged.

R27 yields 1/6 ACCEPT, zero false-safe, four disagreements all ABSTAIN and one all-factor REJECT, but the pre-registered factor_truth_labels_consistent check fails on two cases. V6-F60 records that photo, geometry and semantic truths are intentionally factor-specific; factorized joint truth is their AND, not an equality constraint. R27 stays rejected. R28 tests the corrected product-truth contract over unchanged immutable decisions.

R28 passes product-truth, coverage, risk, strict error-removal, abstention and immutability checks; its unchanged decisions are 1 ACCEPT, 1 REJECT and 4 ABSTAIN with zero false-safe. It remains rejected because the preregistered exact factor-truth disagreement count was guessed as two while full per-factor emission measures three. V6-F61 closes exact diversity frequency as a quality gate. R29 requires diversity to be transparently nonzero and reported while retaining the actual count as an output.

R29 accepts the unchanged six-case actor conjunction with 1 ACCEPT, 1 REJECT, 4 ABSTAIN, zero false-safe and three transparently reported factor-truth disagreements. The accepted area is 49,534 pixels or 17.34% of the actor-mask denominator. R30 now bakes only this appearance evidence into a standalone observation-plane actor asset; because dynamics remains ABSTAIN, it creates no trajectory.

R30 compiles the single R29 ACCEPT into a standalone 49,534-pixel sparse actor appearance payload with exact reload, provenance and photo/geometry/semantic validity. Runtime generator, model, network and source-run payload dependencies are absent. Actor identity remains case-scoped unresolved and no trajectory asset is created because dynamics stays ABSTAIN. R31 now tests two deterministic RGB replays and frozen perception repeatability in that bounded scope.

R31 reconstructs the one R30 actor appearance layer twice with RGB MAE 0, max error 0, exact replay hashes and identical frozen DeepLab label arrays at 394 MiB peak GPU. Full LogSim remains false because identity, 3D pose, novel view and trajectory are unsupported. Since the R7 actor layer can contain multiple actors, R32 does not relabel it directly; it intersects the layer with prior accepted model-index-0 removal support and remeasures all three eligible factors before binding to SceneIR actor_0000.

R32 finds 4,792 actor_0000 pixels with 91.0% support recall and photo ACCEPT at MAE 0.04374. All factor truths are safe, but independent geometry is 0.21218 versus the frozen 0.20 gate and DeepLab/SegFormer semantic consensus is only 0.09833, so the identity-specific conjunction ABSTAINS and H-R32 is rejected. V6-F62 forbids transferring aggregate layer validity to a component. R33 pivots to the honest observed-support baseline by extracting the already accepted H-R13-011 SceneIR actor_0000 Gaussian chunk and logged trajectory without using R30 as identity evidence.

R33 extracts actor_0000/streetgs_actor_0000 as a standalone observed-support bundle with 12,390 exact Gaussian primitives, all seven byte-exact arrays, and 196 exact logged trajectory/visibility/transforms. Provenance and support are complete and the runtime payload has no generator, model, network or source-run dependency. Generated identity recovery remains rejected and class, semantic accuracy, novel dynamics, planning and safety remain abstentions. R34 now tests two deterministic replays from a detached copy of this package.

R34 copies the R33 package into a detached runtime root and produces two byte-identical 196-state actor_0000 replays. All seven Gaussian arrays remain exact, pose quaternions remain normalized to 1.06e-7 error, and logged path length is 196.91 m. This closes state-table replay but not world-space geometry placement, so R35 applies every logged rigid pose to every identity-bound Gaussian and tests geometric invariants before any sensor-render attempt.

R35 deterministically compiles all 12,390 actor_0000 Gaussians through 196 logged poses, producing 2,428,440 world-space primitive states twice with identical hashes. Inverse-pose and centered-radius errors are 4.04e-6 m and 4.11e-6 m; world quaternion norm error is 5.05e-8. This establishes rigid geometry but not rendered sensor equivalence, so R36 now substitutes the standalone payload into the frozen StreetGS full renderer at the two accepted actor-support frames.

R36 replaces native StreetGS actor model index 0 with the standalone compiled actor at frames52/57. All actor fields agree within 1.91e-6, full RGB MAE is at most 6.00e-9, depth MAE at most 2.25e-7 m, and both compiled renders are exact repeats; actor effects cover 30,991 and 13,374 pixels. R37 now moves from logged replay to two explicit counterfactual trajectory translations, comparing compiled and native edit paths without claiming their physical validity.

The first R37 run numerically passed both counterfactual edit paths, but its structured preregistration timestamp was accidentally written as 17:15, later than the 17:05 run start. V6-F63 rejects it as canonical despite the source commit having preceded execution. H-R37-002 uses server UTC 17:12:06, freezes the same method and thresholds without outcome-driven changes, and immediately reruns.

H-R37-002 reproduces the unchanged x/y 1m edit results under valid commit-before-run and server-UTC ordering: 8,182/9,319 changed pixels, full RGB MAE <=3.03e-9, depth MAE <=8.62e-8 m, exact repeats and exact native state restoration.
